function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Reykjavík – the clear winner for an ice‑hockey‑focused trip** | Why Reykjavík stands out | What you’ll find there | |---------------------------|------------------------| | **Home of the national league** – The top‑tier Icelandic Hockey League (IHL) plays its home games at the *Íþróttahúsið* (Sports Hall) in Reykjavík. | • 2–3 games per week during the season (Oct‑Mar).
• Modern indoor rink, good seating, and a lively atmosphere. | | **Largest fan base** – Reykjavík’s population (~130 k) means the crowds are bigger and the rivalry between local teams (e.g., *Íshúsfélagið* and *Hrafninn*) is intense. | • Standing‑room tickets are often cheaper, but you can also get seats for a more comfortable view. | | **Convenient logistics** – The capital has the country’s main airport, plenty of hotels, restaurants, and public transport. | • Easy to combine a game with sightseeing (Harpa, Hallgrímskirkja, Laugavegur shopping street). | | **Ice‑hockey culture** – Reykjavík hosts the annual *Icelandic Cup* and the *All‑Icelandic Championship* finals, drawing fans from across the country. | • You’ll see the best local talent, including players who have played abroad. | | **Accessibility for visitors** – Tickets are sold online in English, and many staff speak English. | • No need to learn Icelandic to enjoy the game. | ### Quick travel tips | Tip | Detail | |-----|--------| | **When to go** | Late October to early March is peak season. Check the IHL schedule on their official site or the *Íþróttahúsið* website. | | **Tickets** | Buy online via the *Íþróttahúsið* portal or at the box office. Prices range from ISK 1,500–3,000 (~$10–$20). | | **Getting around** | Reykjavík’s bus network (Strætó) covers the city and suburbs. Taxis and rideshare apps are also available. | | **Other activities** | Combine a game with a whale‑watching tour, a geothermal spa (Blue Lagoon), or a day trip to the Golden Circle. | --- #### Alternative: Akureyri (Northern Iceland) If you’re willing to travel a bit further, Akureyri hosts the *Akureyri Ice Rink* and the local team *Akureyri Hockey Club*. It’s a smaller venue, but the town’s charm and the friendly atmosphere make it a worthwhile detour. --- **Bottom line:** For the most vibrant ice‑hockey experience, Reykjavík is your best bet. It offers the highest level of play, the biggest crowds, and the easiest travel logistics—all while letting you soak in Iceland’s capital culture. Enjoy the game!
